title: Derek Fisher says Hall of Fame is for the best individual players, not role players
text:
Derek Fisher says Hall of Fame is for the best individual players, not role players
Derek Fisher, a longtime Los Angeles Lakers player, said on Aug. 25 that he understands why he is unlikely to be inducted into the Basketball Hall of Fame. Fisher played 18 seasons in the NBA, including 13 with the Lakers, and was part of five championship teams and seven Finals appearances between 2000 and 2010.
Fisher's role with the Lakers varied from backup point guard to starter across his career. He contributed key plays during playoff runs but did not accumulate significant individual accolades. "The Hall of Fame is rightfully designed for guys that individually are by far the best players that have ever played professional basketball in terms of their production, their stats, their impact," Fisher said on The Joint Venture Show. "It’s different than being part of great teams, in my opinion. I’m OK with it. I know the five championships didn’t just fall into my lap. I know how much I had to do with them. But at the same time, I do recognize there’s a difference between me and Magic Johnson. I should not be in the same room with Magic Johnson."
Fisher never made an All-Star team or an All-NBA team during his career and did not finish among top vote-getters for any major league awards or lead statistical categories except games played.
Despite this lack of personal honors, Fisher remains a popular figure among Lakers fans for his contributions to multiple title-winning teams alongside stars such as Kobe Bryant and Shaquille O’Neal.
In other news related to the Lakers organization, current ownership is facing legal challenges regarding team control as Mark Walter plans to sell his majority stake to Josh Kushner and Bob Iger, while Jeanie Buss contests her family's decision to sell their minority stake.
